One packet's journey, from the wire to the screen.

- Read [`../architecture.md`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) first for the one-screen map of the tree.
- This page is the function-level trace through it.

## The program spine

*Startup is a straight line with exactly one branch.
The shape first, then what each step does.*

<pre class="mermaid">
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Main as main
    participant Cli
    participant Boot as bootstrap
    participant Plan as RunPlan
    participant Mode as run mode entry

    Main-&gt;&gt;Cli: parse_args
    Main-&gt;&gt;Boot: init_logging, run_startup_commands
    Main-&gt;&gt;Boot: block_privilege_escalation (PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS)
    Main-&gt;&gt;Cli: validate
    Main-&gt;&gt;Boot: read_config, declare_node_name
    Main-&gt;&gt;Boot: apply_config
    Main-&gt;&gt;Boot: install_panic_hook
    Main-&gt;&gt;Boot: plan(cli, config)
    Boot--&gt;&gt;Plan: source, capture_config, policy, filter, mode
    alt mode == CoresFile
        Main-&gt;&gt;Mode: run_cores_file (no capture thread)
    else Tui or Batch
        Main-&gt;&gt;Boot: launch(source, capture_config)
        Boot--&gt;&gt;Main: capture handle + PacketRx
        Note over Boot,Main: chroot, privilege drop, runtime hardening
        Main-&gt;&gt;Mode: run_tui_mode or batch::run
    end
</pre>

`main()` is deliberately thin.

- It has ten numbered steps plus four lettered sub-steps, across 171 lines of [`main.rs`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/main.rs).
- Each step delegates to [`app/bootstrap.rs`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/app/bootstrap.rs).

The order matters:

- logging before anything can log
- immediate commands (`--setup-caps`, `--strip-secrets`) before config loading
- `PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS` immediately after them, and before it reads any input
  - `--setup-caps` runs `sudo setcap`.
  - sudo is a setuid binary the flag would break.
- signal handlers and CLI validation before it acquires any resource
- the crash hook armed before the first fallible step
- only then the plan

The hardening step is in `main()` rather than in `launch()`. Two reasons:

- It applies to every run mode.
  That includes the `CoresFile` one that never reaches `launch()`.
- It has no precondition.
  The privilege drop differs: it needs root to do anything at all.

[`plan()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/app/bootstrap.rs) decides *everything* up front and touches nothing. It decides:

- capture-source precedence (`-I file` > `-d device` > config device > `--hep-listen` > auto-detect)
- capture config
- port range
- output and autostop policy
- the compiled filter expression
- the run mode

It starts no capture, changes no privileges, and never exits the process.

- Every fatal misconfiguration comes back as a `PlanError` for `main()` to handle.
- The result is a `RunPlan`.
- `RunPlan::mode` is one of three variants:

| `RunMode` | Entry point | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| `Tui` | [`run_tui_mode()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/app/tui_mode.rs) | Capture thread → channel → `tui-processor` thread → shared stores; main thread renders. |
| `Batch` | [`run()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/app/batch.rs) | Capture thread → channel → the main thread's own receive loop. |
| `CoresFile` | [`run_cores_file()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/app/batch.rs) | No capture thread at all: the file reader shards straight to worker threads. |

`CoresFile` dispatches *before* [`launch()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/app/bootstrap.rs).

- Multi-core file reconstruction owns its own reader.
- So it skips the capture thread, channel, and privilege-drop handshake.

For the other two modes, `launch()` does these in order:

- builds the channel
- starts the capture thread
- waits for the readiness handshake
- chroots, drops privileges, and applies runtime hardening

sipnab sheds privileges after the socket exists and before it parses the first packet.

## The six hops

Every mode is the same six hops.
Only who performs hop 5 (**Apply**) differs.

- **Source.**
  - [`capture/live.rs`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/capture/live.rs),
    [`capture/file.rs`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/capture/file.rs) or
    [`capture/hep.rs`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/capture/hep.rs) produce a `Packet`.
  - Its `data` is a `bytes::Bytes` slice of the captured frame.
  - There is no copy, here or anywhere downstream.
  - A HEP packet arrives pre-parsed.
    - Its addresses, ports and IP protocol number come from HEP chunks.
    - `parse_packet_unstamped` maps the number to a transport in `hep_transport`.
    - `--hep-parse`'s `unwrap_hep` in [`app/batch.rs`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/app/batch.rs) calls it too.
    - Only for a packet a HEP wrapper delivered:
      - 22 reads as TLS and 50 as WS.
        These are the fake numbers OpenSIPS and Kamailio send for decrypted TLS and WebSocket legs.
      - The message's top Via narrows 22, 50 or 6 to WS or WSS.
    - A captured frame never takes that reading.
    - See [How `--hep-listen` reads the transport](@/docs/cli.md#how-hep-listen-reads-the-transport).
  - A stored vCon container read by `-I` arrives pre-parsed too.
    - [`capture/vcon_input.rs`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/capture/vcon_input.rs) rebuilds each stored SIP message as wire text.
    - It sets `PreParsed::vcon`.
      That carries the transport the container named.
      It also makes the parsed packet's origin `InputOrigin::Vcon`.
    - The one detection rule is `sniffs_as_container`: the first byte other than whitespace is `{`.
  - A live device name goes to libpcap untouched.
    - libpcap picks the capture backend from it (`netmap:eth0` selects netmap).
    - So which backends a binary reaches is a property of the libpcap it loads, not of sipnab.
    - [`capture/libpcap.rs`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/capture/libpcap.rs) asks that library at runtime through `pcap_lib_version()`.
    - It reads the banner in one pure function, `parse_banner`.
    - `--version`, the TUI help, MCP `server_capabilities` and REST `GET /v1/capabilities` all report its `running()`.
    - None of them may name a backend the banner does not.
- **Channel.**
  - [`capture::channel`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/capture/channel.rs) moves it to the consumer.
  - It is an unbounded crossbeam channel with a count-capped permit pool.
  - So idle memory returns to ~0.
  - A saturated pipeline still blocks the capture loop rather than growing without bound.
- **Parse.**
  - [`PacketProcessor::process()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/capture/mod.rs) turns one `Packet` into zero or more `ParsedPacket`s.
  - It does link-layer decap, IP defragmentation, TCP reassembly and tunnel unwrapping,
    via [`parse_packet()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/capture/parse.rs).
  - One frame can yield several messages.
    That is why the return type is plural.
  - A HEP message, a uprobe read and a message rebuilt from a vCon skip TCP reassembly.
    - Each is one whole message.
    - Each carries no TCP sequence number for the reassembler to order.
- **Classify.**
  - [`classify_packet()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/pipeline.rs) decides what the packet *means*.
  - It returns a `PacketAction`: `Sip { msg, sdp_links }`, `Rtp { .. }`, `Rtcp(..)` or `None`.
  - All of these happen here:
    - WebSocket-SIP unwrap
    - SDP link extraction via [`extract_sdp_links()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/pipeline.rs)
    - SRTP/DTLS key learning
    - heuristic RTP discovery
  - **It touches no store.**
  - It is not lock-free.
    Three process-global side-tallies each take a mutex when they have something to record:
    - the `--portrange` skip counter
    - the LLMNR store
    - the STUN tracker
- **Apply.**
  - The caller applies that action to its stores:
    [`DialogStore`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/sip/dialog_store.rs) and
    [`StreamStore`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/rtp/stream_store.rs).
  - This is the only hop that differs between paths.
- **Present.**
  - The TUI renders from the stores under `try_read()`.
  - Every serializing surface projects through [`output/model.rs`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/output/model.rs):
    CLI, NDJSON, REST, MCP, TUI save.

## The four appliers

Four call sites apply a `PacketAction`.
All four classify with the same function.

That is the whole point of the split:

- Classification is protocol logic that must not vary.
- Application is store access that legitimately does.

| Path | Applier | Store access |
|---|---|---|
| Live (TUI) | [`process_packet()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/pipeline.rs) | Brief per-store `write()` locks, one store at a time. |
| Batch | [`process_parsed_packet()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/app/batch.rs) | Plain `&mut`, because the receive loop already holds BOTH store write locks for the whole of a packet's processing. That is why `DeferredEffects` exists. |
| `--cores N` | [`reconstruct()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/parallel.rs) | Plain `&mut` on thread-local stores. |
| TUI file open | [`run_pcap_load()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/tui/controllers/file_open.rs) | `write()` locks on the live stores, concurrent with the render thread. |

Before one pipeline replaced four (WS1), each of these carried its own copy of the classification logic.

- They had already drifted.
- Heuristic RTP discovery and WebSocket unwrap worked on some paths and not others.

The rule now is absolute: **a new protocol behavior goes in `classify_packet()`, never in an applier**.

- `PacketAction` is what makes it enforceable.
- An applier that ignores a variant fails to compile once the variant lands.

The live path is the one with locks.
Its ordering is the deadlock-relevant detail.

<pre class="mermaid">
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Cap as capture::live
    participant Ch as capture::channel
    participant Proc as tui-processor
    participant PP as PacketProcessor
    participant Cls as pipeline::classify_packet
    participant DS as DialogStore
    participant SS as StreamStore

    Cap-&gt;&gt;Ch: acquire permit (blocks when full)
    Cap-&gt;&gt;Ch: send Packet (Bytes slice)
    Ch--&gt;&gt;Proc: recv Packet, release permit
    Proc-&gt;&gt;PP: process(&amp;Packet)
    PP--&gt;&gt;Proc: ParsedPackets (decap, frag + TCP reassembly)
    Proc-&gt;&gt;Cls: classify_packet(pp, ..)
    Note over Cls: no store touched — side-tallies take a mutex when they fire
    Cls--&gt;&gt;Proc: PacketAction::Sip { msg, sdp_links }
    Proc-&gt;&gt;DS: write lock
    DS--&gt;&gt;Proc: release
    Proc-&gt;&gt;SS: write lock
    SS--&gt;&gt;Proc: release
    Note over DS,SS: dialog before stream, never both at once
</pre>

## The TUI tick

The render side never blocks on the stores.
One iteration of the loop in [`run_tui_with_pause()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/tui/mod.rs) does these in order:

- polls background work
- refreshes its caches under `try_read()`
- draws
- runs deferred work
- drains every queued input event before the next redraw

The ordering is deliberate at two points:

- Deferred saves and audio playback run *after* the frame that painted their status.
- It drains input in full.
  So a paste burst is not metered out one keystroke per frame.

<pre class="mermaid">
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant UI as TUI event loop
    participant Load as pcap-load worker
    participant App
    participant DS as DialogStore
    participant Term as terminal

    UI-&gt;&gt;Load: poll_pcap_load (progress or completion)
    UI-&gt;&gt;App: drain_async_messages
    UI-&gt;&gt;App: sync_caches
    App-&gt;&gt;DS: try_read
    alt guard acquired
        DS--&gt;&gt;App: snapshot counts and rows
    else contended
        DS--&gt;&gt;App: keep last frame's caches
    end
    UI-&gt;&gt;Term: draw_frame
    Term--&gt;&gt;UI: drew = true or skipped
    opt drew
        UI-&gt;&gt;App: run_pending_save, run_pending_audio
    end
    UI-&gt;&gt;Term: poll(adaptive timeout)
    Term--&gt;&gt;UI: key or mouse events
    UI-&gt;&gt;App: handle every queued event, then loop
</pre>

A skipped frame is not a bug.

- A contended `try_read()` means a writer holds the lock.
- So the frame renders from the previous snapshot.
- The adaptive cadence (10 fps active, 2 fps idle) bounds how stale that can be.
- `draw_frame()` forces a blocking frame after a bounded number of skips.
  So the display cannot freeze.

## `--cores N`

Offline reconstruction shards by **host pair**, not by packet or by call.

- The reader peeks only the link, IP and transport headers.
  - [`peek_frame()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/capture/parse.rs) walks to the outer IP header once and reads the host pair and the UDP or TCP ports there.
  - For a UDP datagram on a `--portrange` port it also checks whether the payload starts a SIP message that names `application/sdp`. That decides whether every worker receives a copy.
  - It does no SIP parse and no allocation.
- Then [`shard_for()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/parallel.rs) maps that pair to a worker.
- The mapping is direction-independent.
  - So a call's request and response legs land on the same worker.
  - That worker rebuilds its bidirectional RTP without any cross-thread coordination.

Each worker owns a private `PacketProcessor` and thread-local stores.

- So the hot path takes no STORE lock.
- The stores merge only at EOF.
- The three process-global side-tallies are the exception.
  - Every worker writes the same one.
  - So a capture that trips one of them often contends on one mutex regardless of worker count.

<pre class="mermaid">
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Reader as file reader
    participant Shard as shard_for
    participant W0 as worker 0
    participant W1 as worker 1
    participant Merge as merged stores

    Reader-&gt;&gt;Shard: peek outer src/dst IP
    Shard--&gt;&gt;Reader: worker index (direction-independent)
    Reader-&gt;&gt;W0: batch of packets (host pair A)
    Reader-&gt;&gt;W1: batch of packets (host pair B)
    Note over W0,W1: thread-local DialogStore + StreamStore, no locks
    W0-&gt;&gt;Merge: merge at EOF
    W1-&gt;&gt;Merge: merge at EOF
    Merge-&gt;&gt;Merge: reassociate_all
    Note over Merge: repairs SDP-to-RTP links split across workers
</pre>

Two dispatch shapes exist.

- [`run_offline_parallel()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/parallel.rs) consumes a `PacketRx` one packet at a time.
- [`run_offline_parallel_file()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/parallel.rs) reads the file itself and sends packets in batches of 128.
  - The reason: the per-packet channel hop capped throughput past two cores.
  - The reconstruction work did not.

The merge is a union, since a host pair belongs to exactly one worker.

- One case is the exception.
  It makes [`reassociate_all()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/rtp/stream_store.rs) necessary.
  - SDP can advertise a media address on a different host pair than the signaling.
  - Then one worker sees the offer and another sees the media.
- Each [`merge()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/rtp/stream_store.rs) carries its endpoints along.
- The re-association pass after merging links those streams to their calls.

## Presentation

Everything that serializes a dialog or a stream goes through [`output/model.rs`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/output/model.rs).

It exists because "dialog summary" was once implemented five times.
Those copies had already drifted on the wire:

- MCP said `message_count` where the CLI and REST API said `msg_count`.
- MCP emitted Debug-formatted `Invite` where the API emitted `INVITE`.

Now one `DialogSummary` and one `StreamSummary` constructor feed all of these alike:
CLI, NDJSON, REST, MCP, TUI save and reports.
[`summary_consistency_test`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/tests/summary_consistency_test.rs) pins it.

These are the *compact* projections.

- The full-fidelity forms live in [`output/json.rs`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/output/json.rs):
  every header, SDP timelines, quality intervals.
- Adding a field to one surface only means adding it to the model.
  That is the point.
